scope: Proposition 5.3 (Localized shear perturbations) of the manuscript “One-sided negative sectional curvature and the holomorphic Liouville property” (preprints/One-sided-negative-sectional-curvature-and-the-holomorphic-Liouville-property-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 359 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dedbbd2f24f8281c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 5.2, suppose E and the center are constant on the spatial region under consideration. Assume also that the first and pure second spatial derivatives of ψ, in the affine coordinates of that proposition, have norms at most eϵE. Add ℓsh = Re(csh(s)(y − ζ)). On the support of its coefficient’s derivatives suppose ψ ≥ −J, where J ≥ 0, and ∥j≤4 csh∥ ≤ e−CE−J/2 . (5.24) For a sufficiently large C depending only on the profile and the constants in the quiet criterion, this perturbation preserves metric positivity and nonpositive real sectional curvature for all y. Moreover its metric is at least one half the unperturbed metric, and fixed fractions of the curvature margins remain. The choice of C is independent of dimension.
